reasoning.text: Reproducibility is mid: every functional parameter (N=1024, q=12289, 14-bit, psi/omega/Ninv, Barrett mu/k, 8 BUs, radix {2,4}, negacyclic) is pinned and both impls converge on a verifiably-correct NTT/INTT engine, but the paper's CENTRAL contribution — the conflict-free bank/offset map, crossbar permutation, rearranged twiddle addressing — is source-missing, so the impls diverge on invented schemes and the FSM is given three contradictory ways. Fidelity is correspondingly capped: the implementations are a faithful negacyclic NTT with the right numbers, yet the conflict-free mapping, no-bit-reversal datapath, twiddle-reuse loop, and all resource/ATP savings (the things that make this CFNTT specifically) are either reproduction-invented or unverifiable in functional code.
gaps: [operation] Exact conflict-free bank-index and offset functions (paper Sec.III) — the central contribution, currently reproduction-invented XOR-fold
[connection] Per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s mapping lanes↔banks
[operation] Twiddle-ROM rearranged-loop addressing f(stage,block) under twiddle-reuse
[control] Single authoritative FSM transition table (three contradictory tables present)
[param] Naive-radix-4 add/sub baseline (assumed 10) anchoring the 20% reduction claim
[operation] Barrett corrected-residual bound / exact conditional-subtract count
[port] Host/PCIe DMA + AXI-Stream framing and beat packing at the I/O boundary
[timing] Pipeline-latency partition (9 = mult3+addsub1+Barrett4+reg1) as a timed/functional schedule, not just a number
[param] Specific 14-bit modulus actually used in the paper (only 'NTT-friendly prime' given; q=12289 is a repro fix)
